messages:
Incident Bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate in prod (region: eu-west-1). PagerDuty paged primary. Auto-created incident #INC-5421.
PagerDuty: @Samir you were paged as primary. Initial severity: P2.
Samir: I'm on it, seeing spike ~03:42 UTC. Errors ~2% of requests, latency bump ~300ms. Traces show increase starting 03:35.
Maya: hi Samir, I'm coming online for the night shift in 5. I can take primary if you want to hand off. Any blockers?
Samir: thanks. Still investigating root cause. Likely model-related or slow KV cache misses in eu pool. I can do a quick handoff — want to be primary?
Maya: yes please. I'll take primary and drive. Can you call out a quick summary + any runbook steps I should follow?
Samir: TL;DR: 5xx + latencies from llm-inference in eu-west-1. Recent rollout: model v2.1.1 rolled 02:55 UTC to dedicated pool. My quick checks:
- error traces show OOM-ish stack in transformer kernel, but not full OOM.
- reroute to fallback model (v2.0.9) reduces errors in test calls.
- autoscaler logs show a short drop in available GPUs 03:33-03:36 (scaled down due to metric noise).
Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.dev/incidents/llm-5xx (steps below)
```
1) Check metrics: kubectl get pods -l app=llm-inference -n prod-eu
2) Check recent deploys: redwoodctl deploy history --env=prod --service=llm-inference
3) If errors correlate with v2.1.1, rollback candidate: v2.0.9 (quick rollback script: redwoodctl deploy rollback --service=llm-inference --to=v2.0.9)
4) If capacity dips: force-scale: redwoodctl scale --pool=eu-dedicated --replicas=6
5) If caller-facing regen issues persist, enable graceful fallback routing: routingctl set fallback-model=v2.0.9
```
Irene: copying runbook. I'll be comms if that's ok — can post an incident bridge + customer-impact note.
Samir: perfect. Maya driving, Irene comms, Jorge you on secondary?
Jorge: I can be secondary, monitoring logs and grabbing heap dumps if needed.
Maya: taking driver. First actions:
- verify whether rollback to v2.0.9 fully mitigates in eu test canary (run smoke against canary route)
- if mitigates, plan a full rollback with minimal blast radius (prefer staged canary -> full).
Maya: running smoke now: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.prod/eu/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"healthcheck"}' | jq .status`
Maya: quick result: canary with v2.0.9 returns 200, baseline v2.1.1 still 5xx. Looks like model rollout is the likely culprit.
Irene: posted incident bridge link https://meet.redwood/bridge/INC-5421 and initial customer-impact note: "Partial failures for EU region: approx 2% of generation requests failing; latency increased for 15% of requests. Teams are investigating."
Samir: noted. Also add we have a coverage gap for APAC oncall tonight — Diego is out. If rollback needs manual node maintenance we'll need an eng-infra handoff.
Maya: understood. I'll coordinate rollback now. Plan:
1) Notify infra if nodes need manual intervention.
2) Rollback v2.1.1 -> v2.0.9 in canary (eu small subset).
3) Monitor 1min error rate and p95 latency for 5 minutes.
4) If green, promote rollback to full.
Maya: executing rollback canary...
Incident Bot: Change detected: deploy rollback started by Maya at 03:51 UTC.
Maya: canary rollback done, monitoring shows errors drop to baseline <0.1% and p95 latency back to normal.
Irene: posted updated status to customers: "Mitigation in progress: rolling back to previous model version; monitoring for impact."
Samir: great. Keep Jorge ready for heap dumps if any pods show OOM. Also note: autoscaler noise — open ticket to tune the metric threshold so it doesn't scale down aggressively.
Jorge: acknowledged. I'll keep log tail on: `rlogs -f service=llm-inference region=eu` and watch for 5xx spikes.
Maya: promoting rollback to full now. ETA ~3m.
Incident Bot: Deploy rollback completed at 03:58 UTC. Post-rollback checks pass.
Irene: updating postmortem template in incident doc, capturing root cause hypothesis (model/kernel regression + autoscaler jitter). I'll also list short-term action items: revert rollout process, add stricter scale-down guard, enable routing fallback by default for risky model rollouts.
Samir: handing over shift to Maya now — you are primary @Maya, Irene is comms, Jorge secondary. Diego is flagged as unavailable for APAC gap; assign follow-up ticket for next-day coverage.
Maya: acknowledged, taking the rest of the shift. I'll monitor for 30m and then close the bridge if stable in 1h.
Irene: I'll keep the incident live updates and prepare a customer-facing post with ETA for RCA.
Jorge: good handoff. Ping me if any heap-dump needed.
Maya: thanks all. leaving one TODO for followup: infra to review autoscaler policy (ticket created: INF-3129).
Samir: thanks team. Closing active run tasks from my side. If anything spikes, re-page as usual. :thumbsup:
